user_stories.story: As a user, I create a log by submitting one multipart request with a description and 1 to 5 photos, and get back the created log.
As a user, I get a clear HTTP error when the description or any photo is invalid, and nothing from that request is stored.
As an operator, I know uploaded files cannot overwrite each other or escape uploads/, and tests never touch the real DB or uploads folder.

acceptance_criteria.c: POST /logs (multipart/form-data) with text field "description" and 1-5 file parts named "photos", all valid, returns 201. Body is JSON containing id, description, photos (list of stored image paths), created_at, updated_at; created_at equals updated_at.
After a 201, the log row (description, timestamps, one photo path per photo) exists in SQLite, and each photo exists as a file under uploads/ at the returned path.
Description missing, empty, or whitespace-only returns 422 and nothing is stored (no row, no files).
Zero photos returns 422. Six or more photos returns 422. 1 and 5 photos succeed (boundaries).
A photo whose extension is not .jpg/.jpeg/.png/.webp returns 422.
A file with an allowed extension but content that is not a valid image (e.g. text bytes, truncated/corrupt data), or whose real format is not JPEG/PNG/WEBP, returns 422.
A photo of exactly 5*1024*1024 bytes (otherwise valid) is accepted; one byte more returns 413.
A request whose total body exceeds a configured limit returns 413. The limit is a named constant in models.py and is at least 5 photos x 5 MiB plus overhead.
If any photo in a request fails validation (type, content, size, count), no files from that request remain in uploads/ and no DB row is created. Likewise if a disk or DB error occurs mid-request.
Unexpected server or disk error returns 500 with no leftover files and no row.

Stored filenames are generated and unique (e.g. random/UUID based, extension derived from validated format); two uploads of the same original filename do not overwrite each other. Original filenames containing path separators, "..", drive letters, or absolute paths never create files outside uploads/.
Tests in backend/tests/test_logs.py cover every criterion above, using a temporary SQLite DB and temporary uploads directory (the real database file and uploads/ are untouched after the test run).

Only the create endpoint is added. No list/get/edit/delete/search, frontend, Docker changes. Files edited are limited to backend/main.py, database.py, models.py, routes.py, tests/test_logs.py (plus requirements.txt only if a missing dependency requires it).

assumptions.a: Endpoint is POST /logs; form field "description", repeated file field "photos". User did not name them.
Description is stored trimmed; validity is judged after trimming. No max length imposed.
Validation uses both extension (case-insensitive) and actual image content; client Content-Type is not trusted alone.
Photo paths are stored relative to the project root (e.g. uploads/xxxx.png) and returned as such.
Body-size limit exact value is the implementer's choice, subject to criterion 8; 413 for it may be raised before or after parsing.
No __init__.py or conftest.py is created; if imports require __init__.py, the implementer records why.
Photo count over 5 is checked as 422 even if the body-size limit is not hit.
Uploads folder and DB location are configurable (e.g. via app wiring/dependency) so tests can redirect them; mechanism is the implementer's call.

edge_cases.e: Description with only tabs/newlines; null-like text is just text and valid if non-blank.
Multiple files with identical original names; original name with "../", "..\\", absolute or drive path, or no name.
Mixed valid and invalid photos: valid ones already written must be cleaned up.
Extension/content mismatch (PNG bytes named .jpg): content must be a valid allowed format; the mismatch policy is documented by the implementer.
Empty (0-byte) file part, empty filename part, or "photos" field sent as a non-file text value: 422.
Oversized photo combined with other errors: status precedence among 413 and 422 should be deterministic and tested.
Uploads folder missing at startup: created, or error is 500 and cleaned.

risks.risk: Streaming vs buffered reads: enforcing 5 MiB and the body limit without loading huge uploads into memory needs care.
FastAPI default validation errors are 422 but the 413 and 500 cases need explicit handling; precedence among them is easy to get inconsistent.
Cleanup on failure must also cover DB failure after files are written (atomicity across disk and SQLite).
Windows file handling (open handles preventing deletion in tests/cleanup) and Pillow decompression-bomb concerns for crafted images.

spec.dependencies: fastapi, uvicorn, python-multipart, pillow, httpx, pytest (all already in requirements.txt); stdlib sqlite3. Files: backend/main.py, database.py, models.py, routes.py, tests/test_logs.py; uploads/ folder.
spec.self_critique: Every story maps to criteria (story 1: 1-2; story 2: 3-10; story 3: 11-12). All criteria are observable via HTTP status, DB rows and directory contents. Biggest uncertainty: the invented endpoint/field names and response shape (POST /logs, "description", "photos"), plus the body-limit value, which the user may have preferred differently; these are recorded as assumptions and are cheap to change.
